title: Mr. PinPin and the Timber Tractor: Production Journal
lead: A standalone woodland adventure, from clean camera plates to the finished story.
statusLabel: Working images and visual reviews; cover approved, story in production.
scope: Original standalone fiction inspired by the friendly farm story, using the main-book camera-first workflow.
eyebrow: Mr. PinPin / Standalone adventures / Camera notebook
sourceNotes: This is new fiction, not a chapter of the original book. The farm story informs the warm friendship and vehicle-discovery rhythm. The beaver replaces the farm bear as the driver for this standalone adventure.

The approved title image fixes the red tractor, yellow crane and main-book PinPin design. Clean locations branch from that visual anchor. The missing bridge boards, windfallen wood and willow-twig joke are story inventions approved in outline.
steps: Write the eighteen-scene story in English, Spanish and Russian.
Generate clean environments using camera position, direction and scene state.
Establish the beaver and PinPin together, then add each scene's full cast directly without colored-limb blocking.
Inspect scale, faces, limb attachments, eyelines, crane/load state and bridge continuity.
Compose vertical reading and explicit print pages, separating joke setup from reveal.
Verify local and published reader, multilingual text and PDF; preserve prompts and all attempts.

shots.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create a clean landscape environment plate, 1536x1024, for the same dimensional children's book as the reference cover. Keep the red tractor's design: red hood and enclosed glass cab, big treaded black tires with red hubs, compact yellow folding log crane behind cab, stake-sided logging trailer. shots.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Reference 2 supplies only PinPin's identity. On the clear earthen patch at lower-left, a friendly chestnut-brown BEAVER sits naturally on his haunches facing right toward PinPin. Beaver has a broad flat paddle tail lying behind him to the left, rounded small ears, wide rounded muzzle, two subtle visible front incisors, and a simple blue canvas work vest without trousers or shoes. His two forepaws rest naturally in front of his belly. He is about 75 cm nose-to-tail-root, a believable animal body rather than a human in costume. PinPin stands just to the beaver's right at about one third the beaver's body length, facing left and looking up at his new friend's face. Compact natural hedgehog: fine brown quills, cream muzzle and belly, short paws, friendly small glossy eyes, four natural limbs with far-side limbs naturally hidden. Both bodies are fully framed and clearly separated, safely away from the stationary wheels. Warm curious greeting through their head tilts. Same detailed dimensional woodland picture-book rendering, soft fur and textured cream highlights. 1536x1024 landscape, one continuous illustration, no text.
